name: Gemfan Hurricane 51466 V2
notes: Gemfan's product page (it blocks automated fetches; read through a search snippet): 3 blades, PC, "Prop Dia:131.8mm", center thickness 6.8 mm, "Center Hole Dia:M5", 4.2 g, "Adaptive Motor:2207-2306 and up". The same page prints "Pitch:3.6inch", which contradicts the 51466 name (5.1 in, 4.66 in pitch) and every retailer list (e.g. https://probots.co.in/gemfan-hurricane-51466-v2-5-inch-propellers-4-pack-yellow.html: "Pitch: 4.66 Inch", "Centre Thickness: 7mm", "Weight: ~4.2g"); 4.66 in is kept. Hub diameter: not published. ct_static and cp_static: TODO(source). Nobody publishes a static test of this propeller with RPM (the old 0.105 / 0.048 had no source), so the thrust model cannot use it: a build fitted with it is blocked with "a record is missing a number the thrust model needs" until a measured test is found.

name: APC B5x4.5E Bullnose
notes: Manufacturer page ("Bullnose - FPV Racing Bundle (5x4.5E and 5x4.5EP)"): "0.18 oz." (5.1 g; the page does not say whether that is one propeller), "Hub Diameter" "0.50 in." (12.7 mm), "Hub Thickness" "0.30 in." (7.62 mm), "5 mm" bore; material not stated; two blades. The old URL (/product/5x4-5ep/) no longer resolves. ct_static and cp_static are APC's OWN COMPUTED performance data, not a measurement: the V = 0 row at 15000 RPM of APC's PER3_5x45E.dat (https://www.apcprop.com/files/PER3_5x45E.dat, header "5x4.5E"; APC publishes no separate bullnose file): Ct 0.1931, Cp 0.1105 (0.1888 / 0.1456 at 1000 RPM, 0.1922 / 0.1127 at 10000 RPM). APC's static predictions are known to run above wind-tunnel measurements, so the thrust is likely optimistic. The earlier claim that UIUC tested it is false: the UIUC database has no APC 5-inch propeller.

name: APC 10x4.5 Multi-Rotor
notes: Manufacturer page (LP10045MR): "0.53 oz." (15.0 g), "Hub Diameter" "0.65 in." (16.5 mm), "Hub Thickness" "0.35 in." (8.9 mm), "Shaft Diameter" "1/4 in." (6.35 mm); material not stated. ct_static and cp_static are APC's OWN COMPUTED performance data, not a measurement: the V = 0 row at 5000 RPM of PER3_10x45MR.dat (https://www.apcprop.com/files/PER3_10x45MR.dat): Ct 0.1070, Cp 0.0398 (Ct 0.106-0.112 and Cp 0.039-0.048 over 1000-15000 RPM). The earlier 0.112 / 0.048 paired the 15000 RPM Ct with the 1000 RPM Cp. UIUC has no APC 10x4.5.

name: APC 9x6 Thin Electric
notes: Manufacturer page: "Product Weight" "0.63 oz." (17.9 g), "Hub Diameter" "0.80 in." (20.32 mm), "Hub Thickness" "0.39 in." (9.91 mm), "Shaft Diameter" "1/4 in." (6.35 mm); material not stated. The earlier 9.9 g, 16 x 8 mm hub and 6 mm bore were not APC's numbers. ct_static and cp_static are the UIUC Propeller Database static test of the APC 9x6E (https://m-selig.ae.illinois.edu/props/volume-1/data/apce_9x6_static_rd0987.txt): CT 0.1145, CP 0.0514 at 4963 RPM (CT 0.110-0.117, CP 0.051-0.054 over 2333-6717 RPM).

name: Gemfan D63 Ducted 3-Blade 63mm
notes: Retailer spec list: "Diameter: 63mm", "Pitch: 3 inch", "Weight: 1.36g", "Shaft Diameter: 1.5mm" (T-mount), "Hub thickness: 4.9mm"; three blades per the part name D63-3. Material not stated on that page. ct_static and cp_static are DERIVED from a measured test table, not published: T-Hobby's Cine25 4S motor test with "GF D63-3" (https://www.ligpower.com/product/cine-25-cinewhoop-motor.html) lists thrust, RPM and shaft torque from 50 % to 100 % throttle (e.g. 100 %: 42061 RPM, 349 g, 0.030 N·m). Ct = T / (ρ n² D⁴) and Cp = 2π n Q / (ρ n³ D⁵) at ρ = 1.225 over the 50-100 % rows give Ct 0.357-0.365 (mean 0.362) and Cp 0.315-0.344 (mean 0.322); those coefficients imply a figure of merit of 0.54-0.55. That test is an open propeller, so no duct effect is in these numbers. The CineLog25 V2 ships with HQProp DT63x4 (4-blade), which has no published test data; this 3-blade D63 is the closest 63 mm ducted prop that does.

name: Gemfan Flash 7040 Tri-Blade
notes: Retailer spec list: "Material: PC", "Weight: 7.9G", "Center Hole Inner Diameter: 5mm", "Paddle Disk Diameter: 178.43mm", 3 blades; pitch 4.0 in from the 7040 model number. ct_static and cp_static are DERIVED, not measured: iFlight's XING2 2809 1250KV test sheet gives "GF 7040" at 100 % throttle as 23.56 V, 30.36 A, 2092 g, but no RPM. RPM is reconstructed with the same first-order motor model dronePhysics.js uses, N = kv (V - I Rm) = 1250 x (23.56 - 30.36 x 0.06546) = 26 966 RPM, shaft power = (N / kv) x I = 655 W (no idle current is published), so Ct = 0.083 and Cp = 0.0331 by construction reproduce iFlight's own full-throttle point through this app's model. Caveats: one data point; iFlight's sheet does not state the blade count of its "GF 7040" (assumed to be this tri-blade); an ESC that does not reach full duty at 100 % would make the true RPM lower and Ct higher. The Chimera7 Pro V2 ships with HQ 7.5x3.7x3 props, which have no published test data.

name: T-Motor P17x5.8 Polished Carbon
notes: Manufacturer page: "17*5.8(431.8*147.3mm)", "2blades-integrated", "26.5±1.5g" (per propeller), "CF+Epoxy", "Thrust Limitation: 7.5kg", "Optimum RPM: 3500~6000". Bolts to the motor's 12 mm two-hole pattern, so no shaft bore is given. ct_static and cp_static are DERIVED from T-Motor's MN4014 KV330 + 17x5.8 test table at 22.2 V (https://store.tmotor.com/product/mn4014-kv330-motor-navigator-type.html), which publishes RPM: Ct = T / (ρ n² D⁴) over the 50-100 % rows gives 0.073-0.078 (mean 0.0755). For Cp, battery watts = back-EMF watts + copper loss is solved for the motor current (back-EMF = RPM / kv, Rm 85 mΩ, ESC treated as lossless), and shaft power = back-EMF x (motor current - 1.1 A idle): Cp 0.024-0.026 (mean 0.0247), implying a figure of merit of 0.65-0.70, which is normal for a large carbon rotor.

name: EOLO CN13x5 Carbon-Nylon Multirotor Prop
notes: Sunnysky's own propeller for the X4112S, tested on its product page as "EOLO CN13*5" (13 in, 5 in pitch; two blades and carbon-nylon from the CN series name, as sold). Finwing's VTBIRD combo calls its lift prop "EOLO 1350", read as this 13x5. Weight, hub and bore: TODO(source), not published (counted as 0 g; the VTBIRD's derived electronics weight already holds its props). ct_static and cp_static are DERIVED from the X4112S KV450 + CN13*5 table at 22.2 V on that page, which publishes RPM: Ct = T / (ρ n² D⁴) over the eleven rows from 500 g to 3020 g gives 0.083-0.091 (mean 0.0859). For Cp, battery watts = back-EMF watts + copper loss is solved for motor current (back-EMF = RPM / 450, Rm 43 mΩ, ESC treated as lossless) and shaft power = back-EMF x (motor current - 0.7 A idle): Cp 0.032-0.035 (mean 0.0332), a figure of merit of about 0.50-0.55. The KV400 table on the same page gives the same thrust-RPM points (Ct mean 0.0853).

name: APC 14x7E Thin Electric
notes: Manufacturer page: "14x7E", diameter 14 in, pitch 7 in, "Product Weight" "1.20 oz." (34.0 g), "Hub Diameter" "0.80 in." (20.32 mm), "Hub Thickness" "0.44 in." (11.18 mm), "Shaft Diameter" "1/4 in." (6.35 mm); material not stated on the page; two blades. ct_static and cp_static are DERIVED from Sunnysky's X3520-III KV560 + APC14*7 table at 22.2 V (http://en.rcsunnysky.com/x-fixedwingseries/57.html), which publishes RPM: over the twelve rows from 500 g to 3500 g (the 66.6 A full-throttle row is left out: it is far past the motor's 40 A rating) Ct = T / (ρ n² D⁴) gives 0.077-0.089 (mean 0.0839) and the battery-watts energy balance (back-EMF = RPM / 560, Rm 23 mΩ, idle 1.1 A, ESC lossless) gives Cp 0.031-0.038 (mean 0.0346). Static coefficients, so they say nothing about the propeller in cruise. Used as the VTBIRD's pusher prop: Finwing names an "EOLO/APC 1480" (14x8); Sunnysky's table covers the APC 14x7, the closest size with published data.
